title: Seeded Molasses Wholemeal Rolls
changes_from_base: Treacle sponge, soaked flax, sunflower and pumpkin seeds, wholemeal flour and a mixed seed crust; overnight rise.
summary: Hearty wholemeal rolls made with a treacle sponge and soaked seeds, slow-risen overnight and crusted with sesame, caraway, cumin and aniseed.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook
cling film or a clean tea towel
baking tray lined with baking paper

steps.title: Sponge
steps.text: In a large bowl dissolve the treacle and yeast in the cool water, then whisk in the white flour to a thick batter. Cover and leave 30 min, until bubbly.

steps.title: Seeds
steps.text: Meanwhile pour boiling water over the flax, sunflower and pumpkin seeds and soak 30 min. Drain in a sieve, rinse under the cold tap and drain well, then stir them into the sponge.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Add the egg, oil, wholemeal flour and salt and mix to a shaggy mass. Knead about 5 min on a lightly floured worktop, until it forms a smooth, slightly tacky ball.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Put the dough in a large oiled container or food bag and refrigerate overnight for a slow rise; or leave it covered at room temperature about 1 h, until doubled.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan). Divide the dough into 15 pieces of about 45 g, roll into tight balls and space them 5 cm apart on the tray. Cover and leave 30-60 min, until puffy (longer if the dough was chilled).

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Brush with the beaten egg, mix the topping seeds and sprinkle them over, then bake 18-22 min, until browned and hollow-sounding underneath; the centre reads about 93 °C. Cool on a rack.

tips: Soaking the seeds stops them stealing water from the dough.
Use the overnight rise if you can; the flavour is noticeably deeper.
Weigh the pieces for evenly sized rolls that bake at the same rate.
storage: Keep in a bread bag for up to 3 days; refresh at 180 °C for 5 min. Freeze for up to 2 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
